title: Web Developer Salary: Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Calculate your web developer salary from hourly rates. Includes 38-hour week, casual loading, super guarantee, and tax estimates. Use our timesheet tool.
salarySummary: For a web developer earning $40 per hour, the annual gross salary is approximately $79,040 based on a 38-hour week, with super and casual loading paid on top.

faqs.q: How is annual salary calculated from hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee, the standard is 38 hours per week. For example, $40/hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $79,040 per year. This is gross pay before tax and super. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to do the calculation.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. If your base rate is $40, the casual rate becomes $50 per hour. The loading is included in your gross pay and super is calculated on the total ordinary earnings (including loading). Our timesheet has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically.

faqs.q: How does super guarantee apply to my hourly rate?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. For a $40/hour employee working 38 hours, the annual super contribution is $9,484.80 (12% of $79,040). Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Web Developer Salary from an Hourly Rate

Whether you are negotiating a contract, comparing job offers, or planning your budget, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is a straightforward calculation. For a **web developer salary**, the key factors are the number of hours per week, the type of employment (permanent or casual), and the superannuation guarantee. This guide explains the formula, the role of the National Minimum Wage and award rates, and how casual loading and super are paid on top.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. We assume a standard full-time week of 38 ordinary hours, as defined by the Fair Work Commission. For example, a web developer earning $45 per hour would have an annual salary of $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920. If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your actual hours and see the annual equivalent.

### Fortnightly Pay and Weekly Comparisons

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same $45/hour example, weekly pay is $1,710, so fortnightly is $3,420. This can help you match your budget to your pay cycle.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the legal minimum for award/agreement-free employees. However, most web developers are covered by a modern award, such as the Professional Employees Award or the Clerks Award, which often have higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) with the exact rates for each classification. Always check the applicable award to ensure you are paid correctly.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you work as a casual web developer, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid sick leave or annual leave. For example, if the base award rate is $30 per hour, the casual rate is $37.50 per hour. **Important:** When using our timesheet, enter the base hourly rate (without loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. The tool will add the 25% automatically. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading. The casual loading is part of your ordinary earnings for superannuation purposes.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% (from 1 July 2026) on your ordinary time earnings. This is paid on top of your gross salary, not deducted from it. For a casual employee earning $37.50 per hour (including loading) for 38 hours, the annual super contribution is 12% of $74,100 = $8,892. The super guarantee has a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year, meaning super is not required on earnings above that cap. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) reference to estimate your total remuneration package.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the tax-free threshold is $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) estimator can show you the net amount after tax and Medicare. Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this basic calculation.

### Web Developer Salary Benchmarks

While award rates provide a floor, many web developers earn above the minimum. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026 (ABS Average Weekly Earnings). That equates to an hourly rate of about $54.83 for a 38-hour week. However, web developer salaries vary widely by experience, location, and industry. For a more tailored estimate, refer to industry surveys or job advertisements, but always verify against the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [reference tables](/data) for award-covered roles.

### Putting It All Together

To calculate your own web developer salary:
1. Determine your base hourly rate (from your award, agreement, or contract).
2. Decide if you are casual – if so, add 25% loading.
3. Multiply by hours per week (typically 38) and by 52.
4. Add 12% super on top of the gross amount.
5. Subtract tax and Medicare to estimate take-home pay.

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page provides a step-by-step guide, and the timesheet tool lets you experiment with different rates and hours. Remember that the annual figure is an estimate; it assumes consistent hours, no unpaid overtime, and no penalty rates or allowances. For precise calculations, consult your employer or a qualified accountant.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
